summary: Gifford Pinchot NF ground-level lookout house by the Summit Guard Station, 1930s, photographed 1937; gone, with a benchmark and anchors reported at the site.

facts.design: Ground-level lookout house with a wood stove; no tower (a ground cab)
facts.status_note: Gone per FFLOS and firelookout.com; the Washington Lookouts page lists it as removed.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)

visit.trail_note: Willhite describes rough forest roads, a parking area north of the site, and several minutes' walk through brush; the lookout location is just above the Bluff Mountain Trailhead.

events.note: Ground cab built in the 1930s; FFLOS Built field reads 1930's (decade only), so no single year is sourced
Osborne panoramic survey team photographed the site and guard station on July 9, 1937
Date registered April 7, 2020 per the FFLOS detail page

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no staffing, fire or NRHP history in any source. The built event year in the brief (1930) is a decade placeholder; see corrections. Willhite's photo captions for 'Remaining anchor' are undated; the story does not date them. Access is described as rough roads and a walk, with no closure or permit noted, but no source states the access level, so no access level is recorded. Willhite's '2017' captions sit on other site photos; the anchor captions carry no date. Brief's Summit GS other name is unverified. No photo URLs captured.
